               ('0403', '6010', SERIAL)]
    need(len(targets) == 1, 'Missing or ambiguous new programmer 2025071717')
    return targets[0]


def command(bit):
    return [str(TOOL), '--usb-serial-num', SERIAL, '-b', 'tangmega138k',
            '-m', '--verbose', str(bit)]


def validate_program_log(raw, returncode):
    """Gowin programSRAM can return void after failure; exit zero alone is weak.

    Require the exact verbose post-program status with DONE_FINAL, correct
    physical ID, and no explicit FAIL/Error diagnostic. Historical auto_boot
    bits describe the previous flash attempt and are not parsed as a FAIL line.
    """
    text = raw.decode('utf-8', errors='replace').replace('\r', '\n')
    statuses = re.findall(r'^after program sram: displayReadReg ([0-9a-fA-F]{8})\s*$', text, re.M)
    ids = re.findall(r'^\s*idcode 0x([0-9a-fA-F]+)\s*$', text, re.M)
    failure = bool(re.search(r'\bFAIL\b|\bError\b|\bERROR\b', text))
    final = int(statuses[-1], 16) if statuses else None
    passed = bool(returncode == 0 and text.startswith('write to ram\n') and
                  ids == ['1081b'] and final is not None and final & 0x2000 and
                  not final & 0x8000f and not failure and 'write to flash' not in text)
    return dict(configuration_completed=passed, returncode=returncode,
                final_status=final, status_done_final=bool(final is not None and final & 0x2000),
                explicit_failure=failure, physical_idcodes=ids,
                proof_scope='tool DONE_FINAL/status; not independent FPGA configuration readback')


def save_json(path, result):
    temporary = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + '.tmp')
    temporary.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n')
    os.replace(temporary, path)


@contextmanager
def deferred_signals():
    """Close the Popen→owner-assignment and child-reaping signal windows."""
    blocked = signal.pthread_sigmask(signal.SIG_BLOCK,
                                    {signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGHUP})
    try:
        yield blocked
    finally:
        signal.pthread_sigmask(signal.SIG_SETMASK, blocked)


class ProgramWatch:
    """Single-thread child supervision, updated by the UART capture loop."""
    def __init__(self, child, log, report, out, deadline, clock=time.monotonic):
        self.child, self.log, self.report, self.out = child, log, report, out
        self.deadline, self.clock, self.observed = deadline, clock, False

    def poll(self, *, enforce=True):
        rc = self.child.poll()
        if rc is not None and not self.observed:
            self.observed = True
            self.report.update(validate_program_log(self.log.read_bytes(), rc))
            self.report['program_finished_unix'] = time.time()
            save_json(self.out/'program_result.json', self.report)
        if enforce:
            if rc is None and self.clock() >= self.deadline:
                raise TimeoutError('SRAM programmer deadline')
            if self.observed and not self.report['configuration_completed']:
                raise RuntimeError('SRAM configuration not confirmed; see program.log')
        return rc

    def reap(self, stop_group):
        """No orphan on ordinary failure/signal; report a kernel-level exception.

        A process stuck uninterruptibly in the kernel cannot be guaranteed to
        exit within userspace deadlines. Never label that cleanup successful.
        """
        try:
            if self.child.poll() is None:
                stop_group(self.child, signal.SIGTERM)
                try:
                    self.child.wait(timeout=2)
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    stop_group(self.child, signal.SIGKILL)
                    self.child.wait(timeout=2)

                self.child.wait(timeout=0)

            self.report['programmer_reaped'] = True
        except BaseException as exc:
            self.report['programmer_reaped'] = False
            self.report['programmer_cleanup_error'] = repr(exc)

    """Capture only a fresh new-board USB enumeration after programming starts.

    If the previous enumeration never disappears/changes, capture is
    inconclusive rather than accepting buffered output from an earlier boot.
    No fallback to 7.3 is permitted. Frozen PassiveUART owns/validates its fd.
    """
    def __init__(self, uart, guard, watch, initial):
        self.uart, self.guard, self.watch, self.initial = uart, guard, watch, initial

    def close(self):

                    # execs a fixed wrapper, which itself execs the pinned ELF.

                                      start_new_session=True,

                                               min(started+seconds, clock()+90), clock)

                    report['programmer_pid'] = child.pid
                    save_json(out/'program_result.json', report)

                    report['fresh_console_observed'] = io.fresh
                    report['fresh_console_identity'] = io.fresh_identity

            finally:

    parser.add_argument('--bit', required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('--sha', required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--out', required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('--seconds', type=float, default=120)
    parser.add_argument('--run', action='store_true')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    bit, out = validate_args(args.bit, args.sha, args.out, args.seconds)
    guard, collector, loader = load_dependencies()
    if not args.run:
        print(json.dumps(dict(prepared=True, hardware_access=False, command=command(bit),
                              bitstream_sha256=args.sha, out=str(out), target_serial=SERIAL,
                              port=str(guard.PORT), seconds=args.seconds, flash_writes=0)))
        return 0
    need(socket.gethostname().split('.')[0] == HOST, 'Wrong execution host')
    scoped_path(bit, ROOT, existing=True)
    checked_file(bit, args.sha)
    checked_file(TOOL, TOOL_SHA)
    checked_file(RUNTIME, RUNTIME_SHA)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    (out/'controller_used.py').write_bytes(Path(__file__).read_bytes())
    def stop(sig, frame):
        raise InterruptedError('Signal ' + str(sig))
    previous = {s:signal.signal(s, stop) for s in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGHUP)}
    try:
        result = run_session(out, bit, args.sha, args.seconds, guard, collector, loader)
    finally:
        for s, handler in previous.items():
            signal.signal(s, handler)
    print(json.dumps({k:result.get(k) for k in ('configuration_completed','log_checks_passed',
                    'game_launch_observed','gpu_tested','powercycle_validated','passed','error')}))
    return 0 if result['passed'] else 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())

    def __init__(self): self.t = 0

        self.guard, self.log, self.finish, self.final_rc = guard, log, finish, rc
        self.returncode = None

        self.written = False

        return self.returncode
    def wait(self, timeout):

        self.reaped = True
        return self.returncode

    def __init__(self, guard):
        self.guard, self.opened, self.sent, self.closes = guard, False, False, 0
    def open(self, timeout=5):

        identity = self.guard.snapshot()
        self.opened = True
        self.guard.events.append(('uart_open', self.guard.clock.now()))
        return identity
    def read(self, n, timeout):

    def close(self):

        self.closes += 1

class Guard:
    PORT = G.PORT
    def __init__(self, clock, *, absent=False, stale=False, old=False, initial=False, interrupt=False):
        self.clock, self.absent, self.stale, self.old = clock, absent, stale, old

        self.locked = False
        self.events = []

    @contextmanager

            assert not self.uart.opened, 'UART must close under lock'

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Root-only flash pre-read coordinator (detect + double read-only backup).

Scope
-----
* One single target: the FTDI 0403:6010 programmer, serial 2025071717, board
  tangmega138k, on host michael-AX15. The 2023112818 dock, UART7.3 and every
  J-Link are forbidden and are never referenced by this file.
* The coordinator only *reads* the SPI flash: one --detect pass and two
  independent --dump-flash passes. It never writes, erases, unprotects or
  bulk-erases the flash. The single --write-flash occurrence is the documented
  non-writing --detect mode, issued without any positional input file.
* Default mode is "prepare": the plan, the pinned identities and the SRAM
  consequence are printed, and no hardware resource, lock or output file is
  opened. "--run" performs the reviewed steps.

Consequence that must stay explicit
-----------------------------------
Preparing a flash access erases the SRAM FPGA configuration of the GW5AST
(reference/src/gowin.cpp:1220). Detect *and* both dumps therefore interrupt
the new SRAM candidate and the Linux it currently runs; afterwards the FPGA
may reload the program already stored in flash. This coordinator never
reloads, restores or re-programs the FPGA and never retries automatically.

Pinned identities
-----------------
wrapper  SHA-256 1c0c245f4bcad2c537b5fbaf77d055c5eccf6b3b17835a24c79be631cd218066
runtime  SHA-256 101c3c17456644f08217c3b11103aa78f8ab4debf4d2d133831c9c91c6d6d873
         (ROOT/runtime/openFPGALoader - never ROOT/bin/runtime/...)
loader   SHA-256 f8387d5a0fa31ba2c832ebb5ed88e0c98594dbb75ad9df9a3321cc9574a970b4
         (ROOT/TESTS/prodock_new_20261028/load_fpga.py, reused through the
         reviewed target_guard context; its main() is never called)
guard    SHA-256 47c4e095d6dab667f8c7d30ecf8c581e9f6bcdf278080242e92ba68616eaff5c
         (reference/target_guard.py beside this module; it is imported only
         after its exact SHA was verified, never through an arbitrary
         sys.path entry)

Runner protocol
---------------
A runner is any callable ``runner(argv, stdout, timeout) -> int`` that writes
the tool output into the already opened binary ``stdout`` file and returns the
process return code (a negative value means death by signal). The default
runner is subprocess with a bounded timeout; it kills and reaps the child
before any exception leaves it, so the global lock is released only after the
tool is really gone. The integration tests inject a fake runner at exactly
this level, so the whole coordinator stays real.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import re
import signal
import socket
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pinned identities and constants (never inferred from the running host).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT = Path('/home/michael/console-validation-20261001')
TOOL_SHA = '1c0c245f4bcad2c537b5fbaf77d055c5eccf6b3b17835a24c79be631cd218066'
RUNTIME_SHA = '101c3c17456644f08217c3b11103aa78f8ab4debf4d2d133831c9c91c6d6d873'
LOADER_SHA = 'f8387d5a0fa31ba2c832ebb5ed88e0c98594dbb75ad9df9a3321cc9574a970b4'
GUARD_SHA = '47c4e095d6dab667f8c7d30ecf8c581e9f6bcdf278080242e92ba68616eaff5c'
#: The reviewed guard is imported from this exact relative location only.
GUARD_RELATIVE = Path('reference') / 'target_guard.py'

SERIAL = '2025071717'
VENDOR = '0403'
PRODUCT = '6010'
BOARD = 'tangmega138k'
EXPECTED_IDCODE = '1081b'          # GW5AST-138 physical ID of tangmega138k
HOST_REQUIRED = 'michael-AX15'

SECTOR_BYTES = 65536               # capacity = sectors * 65536
DETECT_TIMEOUT = 120               # seconds, default detect timeout
DUMP_TIMEOUT = 900                 # seconds, default timeout of each dump
MIN_TIMEOUT = 1
MAX_TIMEOUT = 1800

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Log grammar of openFPGALoader v1.1.1 (exact known shapes).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
JEDEC_RE = re.compile(r'^[ \t]*JEDEC ID:[ \t]*0x([0-9a-fA-F]{6})[ \t]*$', re.MULTILINE)
JEDEC_ANY_RE = re.compile(r'^[ \t]*JEDEC[ \t]+ID[ \t]*:[ \t]*(\S*)[ \t]*$',
                           re.MULTILINE | re.IGNORECASE)
DETECTED_RE = re.compile(
    r'^(?P<model>.+?)[ \t]+(?P<sectors>\d+)[ \t]+sectors[ \t]+size:[ \t]*'
    r'(?P<size>\d+(?:\.\d+)?)[ \t]*Mb(?:its)?[ \t]*$', re.IGNORECASE)
FOUND_RE = re.compile(r'^[ \t]*found[ \t]+(\d+)[ \t]+devices[ \t]*$', re.MULTILINE)
INDEX_RE = re.compile(r'^[ \t]*index[ \t]+(\d+)[ \t]*:[ \t]*$', re.MULTILINE)
IDCODE_RE = re.compile(r'^[ \t]*idcode[ \t]+0x([0-9a-fA-F]+)[ \t]*$', re.MULTILINE)
DETECT_MARK_RE = re.compile(r'^[ \t]*Detect flash:[ \t]*$', re.MULTILINE)
DETECTED_LINE_RE = re.compile(r'^[ \t]*Detected:[ \t]*(.*)$', re.MULTILINE)

# Records that describe the device or the flash; nothing like them may follow
# the completion line.
SIGNIFICANT_RES = (FOUND_RE, INDEX_RE, IDCODE_RE, DETECT_MARK_RE,
                   JEDEC_ANY_RE, DETECTED_LINE_RE)

# A display error makes the pass a failure. Whole words, case insensitive.
ERROR_PATTERN = re.compile(r'\b(?:fail|failed|failure|error|errors)\b', re.IGNORECASE)
# Historical flag text of an earlier trial: not an error of this pass.
HISTORICAL_FLAG = re.compile(r'auto_boot_1st_fail', re.IGNORECASE)

# Dump completion markers, in the order the tool prints them.
DUMP_MARKERS = (
    ('dump flash (May take time)', re.compile(r'dump flash\s*\(\s*may take time\s*\)',
                                              re.IGNORECASE)),
    ('Open dump file DONE', re.compile(r'open dump file\s+done', re.IGNORECASE)),
    ('Read flash', re.compile(r'read flash', re.IGNORECASE)),
    ('100.00%', re.compile(r'100\.00\s*%')),
)
WRITE_TO_FLASH_RE = re.compile(r'write to flash', re.IGNORECASE)

CONSEQUENCES = (
    'Flash access erases the SRAM FPGA configuration on GW5AST-138 '
    '(reference/src/gowin.cpp:1220): the new SRAM candidate and the Linux it '
    'currently runs stop during the detect step and during both dumps.',
    'After that interruption the FPGA may reload the program currently stored '
    'in flash; this coordinator never reloads, restores or re-programs it.',
    'No flash write, erase, unprotect or bulk-erase command is issued. The only '
    '--write-flash flag used is the documented non-writing --detect mode, '
    'without any positional input file.',
    'Root cleanup of partial logs and partial dumps stays a separate root '
    'decision: every artifact is kept and nothing is deleted or restored here.',
)


class FlashError(ValueError, RuntimeError, OSError):
    """Refusal of the pure API or of the coordinator.

    It derives from ValueError, RuntimeError and OSError so that a caller may
    catch whichever of those it expects for a rejected input.
    """


class _Abort(BaseException):
    """Raised from a signal handler so the finally block still writes JSON."""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small helpers.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _as_text(raw):
    """Decode a log to text without ever raising on odd bytes."""
    if isinstance(raw, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
        return bytes(raw).decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    return str(raw)


def sha256_file(path):
    """SHA-256 of a regular file, read in chunks."""
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, 'rb') as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1 << 20), b''):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def _error_context(text):
    """Return the offending snippet of an error word, or None."""
    cleaned = HISTORICAL_FLAG.sub(' ', text)
    match = ERROR_PATTERN.search(cleaned)
    if not match:
        return None
    start = max(0, match.start() - 40)
    return cleaned[start:match.end() + 40].strip()


def _require_regular(path, what):
    """Refuse symlinks and non regular files; return the lstat result."""
    try:
        info = os.lstat(path)
    except OSError as error:
        raise FlashError('%s is not accessible: %r' % (what, error))
    if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):
        raise FlashError('%s is a symlink: %s' % (what, path))
    if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
        raise FlashError('%s is not a regular file: %s' % (what, path))
    return info


def _is_significant(line):
    """True when a line carries a device or a flash record."""
    return any(pattern.search(line) for pattern in SIGNIFICANT_RES)


def _check_done(lines, what):
    """Require the single "Done" completion line; return its line index.

    Only annotations may follow it (a historical "auto_boot_1st_fail" flag of
    an earlier trial is such an annotation, not an error).
    """
    done = [index for index, line in enumerate(lines) if line.strip() == 'Done']
    if not done:
        raise FlashError('%s: missing final "Done" line' % what)
    if len(done) != 1:
        raise FlashError('%s: repeated "Done" line' % what)
    for line in lines[done[0] + 1:]:
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if _is_significant(line):
            raise FlashError('%s: a device or flash record follows the "Done" line'
                             % what)
    return done[0]


def _check_idcode(text, what):
    """One physical ID, and it must be the GW5AST-138 of tangmega138k."""
    codes = IDCODE_RE.findall(text)
    if len(codes) != 1:
        raise FlashError('%s: expected exactly one physical idcode, got %d'
                         % (what, len(codes)))
    code = codes[0].lower()
    if code != EXPECTED_IDCODE:
        raise FlashError('%s: unexpected physical idcode 0x%s (expected 0x%s)'
                         % (what, code, EXPECTED_IDCODE))
    return code


def _check_physical_header(text, what):
    """Exactly one "found 1 devices", one "index 0:" and one idcode 1081b."""
    found = FOUND_RE.findall(text)
    if len(found) != 1:
        raise FlashError('%s: expected exactly one "found N devices" header' % what)
    if int(found[0]) != 1:
        raise FlashError('%s: exactly one physical device expected, got %s'
                         % (what, found[0]))
    indexes = INDEX_RE.findall(text)
    if len(indexes) != 1 or indexes[0] != '0':
        raise FlashError('%s: expected exactly one "index 0:" record' % what)
    return _check_idcode(text, what)


def _parse_detected(line, what):
    """Parse one "Detected: <model> <n> sectors size: <x>Mb" record."""
    match = DETECTED_RE.match(line.strip())
    if not match:
        raise FlashError('%s: unreadable flash geometry record: %r' % (what, line))
    model = match.group('model').strip()
    if not model:
        raise FlashError('%s: empty flash model text' % what)
    sectors = int(match.group('sectors'))
    if sectors <= 0:
        raise FlashError('%s: invalid sector count %d' % (what, sectors))
    size = float(match.group('size'))
    if abs(size - sectors / 2.0) > 1e-9:
        raise FlashError('%s: sector count %d disagrees with displayed size %sMb'
                         % (what, sectors, match.group('size')))
    return model, sectors, size


def _marker_line(text, pattern):
    """Line index of the first match of `pattern`, or None."""
    match = pattern.search(text)
    if not match:
        return None
    return text.count('\n', 0, match.start())


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pure API required by the protected tests.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def parse_detection(raw):
    """Parse a detect log into {jedec, model, sectors, capacity}.

    Raises FlashError (ValueError/RuntimeError/OSError) for an unknown chip, an
    ambiguous or repeated record, a wrong or multiple physical ID, a geometry
    mismatch or any error word in the log.
    """
    text = _as_text(raw)
    lines = text.splitlines()
    what = 'detect log'

    context = _error_context(text)
    if context:
        raise FlashError('%s reports an error status: %r' % (what, context))

    _check_physical_header(text, what)

    if len(DETECT_MARK_RE.findall(text)) != 1:
        raise FlashError('%s: missing or repeated "Detect flash:" marker' % what)

    jedec_any = JEDEC_ANY_RE.findall(text)
    if len(jedec_any) != 1:
        raise FlashError('%s: expected exactly one JEDEC ID record' % what)
    jedec_match = JEDEC_RE.findall(text)
    if len(jedec_match) != 1:
        raise FlashError('%s: unsupported flash identification %r'
                         % (what, jedec_any[0]))
    jedec = jedec_match[0].lower()

    detected = DETECTED_LINE_RE.findall(text)
    if len(detected) != 1:
        raise FlashError('%s: expected exactly one "Detected:" flash record' % what)
    model, sectors, _size = _parse_detected(detected[0], what)

    done_line = _check_done(lines, what)
    if _marker_line(text, DETECTED_LINE_RE) >= done_line:
        raise FlashError('%s: the flash record does not precede the "Done" line'
                         % what)

    return {'jedec': jedec, 'model': model, 'sectors': sectors,
            'capacity': sectors * SECTOR_BYTES}


def parse_dump_log(raw, jedec=None, sectors=None):
    """Check a dump log: identification, geometry, errors and completion.

    A dump log must carry exactly one "found 1 devices" header, one
    "index 0:" record, the physical idcode 1081b, one JEDEC ID record and one
    "Detected:" geometry record. The identification may not be omitted, it
    must match the detection and the completion must follow the read progress.
    """
    text = _as_text(raw)
    lines = text.splitlines()
    what = 'dump log'

    context = _error_context(text)
    if context:
        raise FlashError('%s reports an error status: %r' % (what, context))
    if WRITE_TO_FLASH_RE.search(text):
        raise FlashError('%s mentions a flash write: refusing a read-only dump' % what)

    _check_physical_header(text, what)

    jedec_any = JEDEC_ANY_RE.findall(text)
    if len(jedec_any) != 1:
        raise FlashError('%s: expected exactly one JEDEC ID record' % what)
    jedec_match = JEDEC_RE.findall(text)
    if len(jedec_match) != 1:
        raise FlashError('%s: unsupported flash identification %r'
                         % (what, jedec_any[0]))
    observed = jedec_match[0].lower()
    if jedec is not None and observed != str(jedec).strip().lower():
        raise FlashError('%s: JEDEC %s differs from the detected %s'
                         % (what, observed, jedec))

    detected = DETECTED_LINE_RE.findall(text)
    if len(detected) != 1:
        raise FlashError('%s: expected exactly one "Detected:" flash record' % what)
    model, observed_sectors, _size = _parse_detected(detected[0], what)
    if sectors is not None and observed_sectors != int(sectors):
        raise FlashError('%s: %d sectors differ from the detected %s'
                         % (what, observed_sectors, sectors))

    done_line = _check_done(lines, what)
    for label, pattern in DUMP_MARKERS:
        index = _marker_line(text, pattern)
        if index is None:
            raise FlashError('%s: missing completion marker %r' % (what, label))
        if index >= done_line:
            raise FlashError('%s: the marker %r does not precede the "Done" line'
                             % (what, label))

    return {'jedec': observed, 'model': model, 'sectors': observed_sectors,
            'capacity': observed_sectors * SECTOR_BYTES}


def backup_summary(path, capacity):
    """Return {bytes, sha256} for a regular, non symlink dump of `capacity`."""
    if not isinstance(capacity, int) or isinstance(capacity, bool) or capacity <= 0:
        raise FlashError('invalid capacity: %r' % (capacity,))
    target = Path(path)
    info = _require_regular(target, 'dump file')
    if info.st_size != capacity:
        raise FlashError('dump file %s holds %d bytes, expected %d'
                         % (target, info.st_size, capacity))
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    read = 0
    with open(target, 'rb') as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1 << 20), b''):
            digest.update(chunk)
            read += len(chunk)
    if read != capacity:
        raise FlashError('dump file %s yielded %d bytes, expected %d'
                         % (target, read, capacity))
    return {'bytes': read, 'sha256': digest.hexdigest()}


def compare_backups(a, b, capacity):
    """Compare two independent dumps; raise unless they are truly equal."""
    first = backup_summary(a, capacity)
    second = backup_summary(b, capacity)
    left = os.stat(a)
    right = os.stat(b)
    if left.st_dev == right.st_dev and left.st_ino == right.st_ino:
        raise FlashError('both paths share one inode (%d): not two independent dumps'
                         % left.st_ino)
    if first['sha256'] != second['sha256']:
        raise FlashError('backup contents differ (%s != %s)'
                         % (first['sha256'], second['sha256']))
    if Path(a).read_bytes() != Path(b).read_bytes():
        raise FlashError('backup bytes differ although the digests match')
    return {'matching': True, 'bytes': first['bytes'], 'sha256': first['sha256'],
            'sha256_b': second['sha256'], 'same_inode': False}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reviewed command construction and hardware guard.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load_target_guard(module_dir=None):
    """Import the immutable reviewed guard after verifying its exact SHA.

    Only reference/target_guard.py beside this module is accepted: no
    sys.path import, no other copy and no silent fallback to a locally built
    command. The SHA is checked *before* the module is executed.
    """
    base = Path(module_dir) if module_dir is not None else Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    path = base / GUARD_RELATIVE
    try:
        info = os.lstat(path)
    except OSError as error:
        raise FlashError('the reviewed guard %s is missing: %r' % (path, error))
    if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode) or not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
        raise FlashError('the reviewed guard %s is not a regular file' % path)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    if digest != GUARD_SHA:
        raise FlashError('the reviewed guard %s has SHA %s, expected %s'
                         % (path, digest, GUARD_SHA))
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reviewed_target_guard', path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def _local_command(action, tool, output=None, size=None):
    """The allowlisted argv, built locally (cross check of the guard)."""
    base = [str(tool), '--usb-serial-num', SERIAL, '-b', BOARD, '--verbose']
    if action == 'detect':
        return base + ['--write-flash', '--detect']
    if action == 'dump' and output is not None and isinstance(size, int) and size > 0:
        return base + ['--dump-flash', '--file-size', str(size), str(output)]
    raise FlashError('invalid operation or arguments')


def build_command(action, tool, output=None, size=None):
    """Return the reviewed argv, taken from the reviewed helper itself."""
    guard = load_target_guard()
    try:
        shared = guard.command(tool, action, output=output, size=size)
    except Exception as error:              # the helper refuses bad arguments
        raise FlashError('the reviewed helper refused the command: %r' % error)
    argv = [str(item) for item in shared]
    if argv != _local_command(action, tool, output=output, size=size):
        raise FlashError('the reviewed helper command differs from the allowlisted argv')
    return argv


def default_guard_factory(root):
    """Hold the reviewed global lock around the reviewed steps."""
    root = Path(root)
    tool = root / 'bin' / 'openFPGALoader'
    runtime = root / 'runtime' / 'openFPGALoader'
    loader = root / 'TESTS' / 'prodock_new_20261028' / 'load_fpga.py'
    guard = load_target_guard()
    return guard.guarded_target(tool, TOOL_SHA, loader, LOADER_SHA,
                                runtime=runtime, runtime_sha=RUNTIME_SHA)


def default_runner(argv, stdout, timeout):
    """Run with the pinned SRAM coordinator signal guard and bounded reaping."""
    from process_guard import run_programmer
    return run_programmer(argv, stdout, timeout)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Coordinator.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
class Coordinator:
    """Detect pass, or two read-only dumps bound to a validated detection."""

    def __init__(self, *, phase, out_dir, root=ROOT, timeout=None, runner=None,
                 guard_factory=None, detection=None, detection_sha=None,
                 jedec=None, capacity=None):
        if phase not in ('detect', 'dump'):
            raise FlashError('phase must be detect or dump')
        if timeout is not None and not (MIN_TIMEOUT <= timeout <= MAX_TIMEOUT):
            raise FlashError('timeout must be between %d and %d seconds'
                             % (MIN_TIMEOUT, MAX_TIMEOUT))
        self.phase = phase
        self.root = Path(root)
        self.out_dir = Path(out_dir)
        self.timeout = timeout
        self.runner = runner or default_runner
        self.guard_factory = guard_factory
        self.detection = detection
        self.detection_sha = detection_sha
        self.jedec = jedec
        self.capacity = capacity
        self._out = None            # the output directory this run owns
        self._owns_out = False      # True only when this run created it
        self._programmer_attempted = False  # Runner boundary entered, not FPGA state observed

    # -- paths ------------------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def tool(self):
        return self.root / 'bin' / 'openFPGALoader'

    @property
    def runtime(self):
        # The runtime binary lives beside the wrapper, never below bin/.
        return self.root / 'runtime' / 'openFPGALoader'

    @property
    def loader(self):
        return self.root / 'TESTS' / 'prodock_new_20261028' / 'load_fpga.py'

    def _timeout_for(self, phase):
        if self.timeout is not None:
            return self.timeout
        return DETECT_TIMEOUT if phase == 'detect' else DUMP_TIMEOUT

    def _checked_out_dir(self):
        """Resolve the output directory under ROOT/TESTS, refusing symlinks."""
        out = self.out_dir
        if out.is_absolute():
            try:
                relative = out.relative_to(self.root)
            except ValueError:
                raise FlashError('the output directory must live under %s'
                                 % (self.root / 'TESTS'))
        else:
            relative = out
        if not relative.parts:
            raise FlashError('the output directory is empty')
        if '..' in relative.parts:
            raise FlashError('the output directory must not contain ".." components')
        if relative.parts[0] != 'TESTS':
            raise FlashError('the output directory must live under %s'
                             % (self.root / 'TESTS'))
        current = self.root
        for part in relative.parts:
            current = current / part
            if current.is_symlink():
                raise FlashError('refusing the symlinked output component %s' % current)
        return self.root / relative

    # -- prepare ----------------------------------------------------------
    def prepare(self):
        """Describe the reviewed steps. No hardware, lock or file is opened."""
        out = self._checked_out_dir()
        plan = {
            'phase': self.phase,
            'mode': 'prepare',
            'will_run': False,
            'root': str(self.root),
            'out_dir': str(out),
            'tool': str(self.tool),
            'tool_sha256': TOOL_SHA,
            'runtime': str(self.runtime),
            'runtime_sha256': RUNTIME_SHA,
            'loader': str(self.loader),
            'loader_sha256': LOADER_SHA,
            'target_serial': SERIAL,
            'host_required': HOST_REQUIRED,
            'host_observed': socket.gethostname(),
            'timeouts': {'detect': self._timeout_for('detect'),
                         'dump': self._timeout_for('dump')},
            'flash_writes': 0,
            'sram_interrupt_expected': True, 'programmer_attempted': False,
            'boot': False,
            'gpu': False,
            'powercycle': False,
            'consequences': list(CONSEQUENCES),
            'notes': [
                'The prepare step opens no resource and starts no process.',
                '--run is required for any hardware access.',
                'Every command is built by the reviewed target_guard helper.',
            ],
        }
        if socket.gethostname().split('.')[0] != HOST_REQUIRED:
            plan['notes'].append('The observed host is not %s; the reviewed '
                                 'guard will refuse the run.' % HOST_REQUIRED)
        if self.phase == 'detect':
            plan['commands'] = [build_command('detect', self.tool)]
            plan['outputs'] = ['detect.log', 'detect.json']
        else:
            evidence = self.validate_detection()
            capacity = evidence['parsed']['capacity']
            plan['detection'] = evidence['summary']
            plan['commands'] = [
                build_command('dump', self.tool, output=out / 'backup_a.bin',
                              size=capacity),
                build_command('dump', self.tool, output=out / 'backup_b.bin',
                              size=capacity),
            ]
            plan['outputs'] = ['backup_a.bin', 'backup_a.log', 'backup_b.bin',
                               'backup_b.log', 'dump.json']
            plan['notes'].append('Both dumps run inside one single global lock.')
        return plan

    # -- evidence ---------------------------------------------------------
    def validate_detection(self):
        """Validate the detection JSON, its log SHA and reparse the log."""
        if self.detection is None or self.detection_sha is None:
            raise FlashError('the dump phase requires --detection and --detection-sha')
        if self.jedec is None or self.capacity is None:
            raise FlashError('the dump phase requires --jedec and --capacity')
        path = Path(self.detection)
        _require_regular(path, 'detection file')
        actual = sha256_file(path)
        if actual != str(self.detection_sha).strip().lower():
            raise FlashError('detection file SHA mismatch: %s != %s'
                             % (actual, self.detection_sha))
        try:
            data = json.loads(path.read_text())
        except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
            raise FlashError('detection file is not readable JSON: %r' % error)
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            raise FlashError('detection file is not a JSON object')
        if data.get('phase') != 'detect':
            raise FlashError('detection file phase is %r, expected "detect"'
                             % data.get('phase'))
        if data.get('passed') is not True:
            raise FlashError('the detection pass is not marked as passed')
        self._check_target(data.get('target'))
        if data.get('returncode') != 0 or data.get('flash_writes') != 0:
            raise FlashError('Detection exit/status contradicts successful read-only phase')
        if data.get('loader_sha256') != LOADER_SHA:
            raise FlashError('Detection loader SHA differs')
        if data.get('tool_sha256') != TOOL_SHA:
            raise FlashError('detection tool SHA is not the pinned wrapper SHA')
        if data.get('runtime_sha256') != RUNTIME_SHA:
            raise FlashError('detection runtime SHA is not the pinned runtime SHA')
        log_path = data.get('log')
        log_sha = data.get('log_sha256')
        if not log_path or not log_sha:
            raise FlashError('the detection file does not reference its log')
        log_file = Path(log_path)
        _require_regular(log_file, 'detection log')
        if sha256_file(log_file) != str(log_sha).strip().lower():
            raise FlashError('the referenced detection log SHA does not match')
        parsed = parse_detection(log_file.read_bytes())
        if any(data.get(key) != parsed[key] for key in ('jedec', 'model', 'sectors', 'capacity')):
            raise FlashError('Recorded flash geometry contradicts its log')
        if parsed['jedec'] != str(self.jedec).strip().lower():
            raise FlashError('JEDEC %s differs from the detected %s'
                             % (self.jedec, parsed['jedec']))
        if parsed['capacity'] != int(self.capacity):
            raise FlashError('capacity %s differs from the sector derived %d'
                             % (self.capacity, parsed['capacity']))
        summary = {'path': str(path), 'sha256': actual, 'log': str(log_file),
                   'log_sha256': str(log_sha).strip().lower(),
                   'jedec': parsed['jedec'], 'model': parsed['model'],
                   'sectors': parsed['sectors'], 'capacity': parsed['capacity']}
        return {'parsed': parsed, 'summary': summary}

    @staticmethod
    def _check_target(target):
        """The recorded target identity must be the reviewed one."""
        if not isinstance(target, dict):
            raise FlashError('the detection file does not carry the target identity')

        def pick(*names):
            for name in names:
                if target.get(name) not in (None, ''):
                    return str(target[name])
            return None

        serial = pick('serial', 'target_serial', 'targetSerial')
        vendor = pick('idVendor', 'vendor', 'id_vendor')
        product = pick('idProduct', 'product', 'id_product')
        if serial != SERIAL:
            raise FlashError('the detection targets serial %r, expected %s'
                             % (serial, SERIAL))
        if vendor != VENDOR or product != PRODUCT:
            raise FlashError('the detection targets %s:%s, expected %s:%s'
                             % (vendor, product, VENDOR, PRODUCT))
        board = pick('board', 'target_board')
        if board is not None and board != BOARD:
            raise FlashError('the detection targets board %r, expected %s'
                             % (board, BOARD))

    # -- execution --------------------------------------------------------
    def _base_result(self):
        return {'phase': self.phase, 'mode': 'run', 'passed': False,
                'root': str(self.root), 'out_dir': str(self.out_dir),
                'target_serial': SERIAL, 'board': BOARD,
                'host': socket.gethostname(),
                'tool': str(self.tool), 'tool_sha256': TOOL_SHA,
                'runtime': str(self.runtime), 'runtime_sha256': RUNTIME_SHA,
                'loader': str(self.loader), 'loader_sha256': LOADER_SHA,
                'returncode': None, 'flash_writes': 0, 'sram_interrupt_expected': True, 'programmer_attempted': False,
                'boot': False, 'gpu': False, 'powercycle': False,
                'started_unix': time.time()}

    def _open_guard(self):
        if self.guard_factory is not None:
            return self.guard_factory()
        return default_guard_factory(self.root)

    def _make_out_dir(self, out):
        """Create the exclusive output directory and remember that we own it."""
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        try:
            out.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
        except FileExistsError:
            raise FlashError('the output directory already exists: %s '
                             '(its existing evidence is left untouched)' % out)
        except OSError as error:
            raise FlashError('cannot create the output directory %s: %r'
                             % (out, error))
        self._out = out
        self._owns_out = True

    def _run_logged(self, argv, log_path, timeout, info):
        """Run one reviewed command, keeping the full log and partial output."""
        info.update({'command': [str(item) for item in argv],
                     'log': str(log_path), 'returncode': None,
                     'timeout': False, 'error': None})
        try:
            handle = open(log_path, 'xb')
        except FileExistsError:
            raise FlashError('refusing to overwrite the existing log %s' % log_path)
        except OSError as error:
            raise FlashError('cannot create the log %s: %r' % (log_path, error))
        try:
            try:
                self._programmer_attempted = True
                info['returncode'] = int(self.runner(list(argv), handle, timeout))
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                info['timeout'] = True
                info['error'] = 'timeout after %ss' % timeout
            except BaseException as error:
                # The attempted command stays recorded even when the runner
                # itself failed; the partial log is kept on disk.
                info['error'] = repr(error)
                raise
            finally:
                try:
                    handle.flush()
                    handle.close()
                except OSError:
                    pass
        finally:
            if os.path.exists(log_path):
                info['log_sha256'] = sha256_file(log_path)
        return info

    def _write_result(self, result):
        """Write the result JSON; a failed write may never keep a success."""
        result['programmer_attempted'] = self._programmer_attempted
        if not self._owns_out:
            result['result_json'] = None
            result['result_json_skipped'] = ('the output directory was not '
                                             'created by this run')
            return False
        name = 'detect.json' if self.phase == 'detect' else 'dump.json'
        path = self._out / name
        result['result_json'] = str(path)
        try:
            payload = json.dumps(result, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + '\n'
            with open(path, 'x') as handle:
                handle.write(payload)
        except (OSError, TypeError, ValueError) as error:
            # The provenance of this run is lost: the run is not a success.
            result['passed'] = False
            result['result_write_error'] = repr(error)
            return False
        return True

    def execute(self):
        """Run the phase; the result JSON is always finished in a finally."""
        if self.phase == 'detect':
            return self._execute_detect()
        return self._execute_dump()

    def _execute_detect(self):
        result = self._base_result()
        try:
            out = self._checked_out_dir()
            self._make_out_dir(out)
            with self._open_guard() as identity:
                result['target'] = _identity(identity)
                argv = build_command('detect', self.tool)
                log = out / 'detect.log'
                info = {'command': list(argv), 'log': str(log),
                        'returncode': None, 'timeout': False, 'error': None}
                result['run'] = info
                self._run_logged(argv, log, self._timeout_for('detect'), info)
                result['returncode'] = info['returncode']
                result['log'] = str(log)
                result['log_sha256'] = info.get('log_sha256')
                if info['error']:
                    raise FlashError('detect: %s' % info['error'])
                if info['returncode'] != 0:
                    raise FlashError('detect exited with %s' % info['returncode'])
                parsed = parse_detection(log.read_bytes())
                result['jedec'] = parsed['jedec']
                result['model'] = parsed['model']
                result['sectors'] = parsed['sectors']
                result['capacity'] = parsed['capacity']
                result['passed'] = True
        except BaseException as error:
            result['error'] = repr(error)
            result['passed'] = False
        finally:
            result['finished_unix'] = time.time()
            self._write_result(result)
        return result

    def _execute_dump(self):
        result = self._base_result()
        result['dumps'] = {}
        try:
            evidence = self.validate_detection()
            result['detection'] = evidence['summary']
            result['jedec'] = evidence['parsed']['jedec']
            result['model'] = evidence['parsed']['model']
            result['sectors'] = evidence['parsed']['sectors']
            result['capacity'] = evidence['parsed']['capacity']
            out = self._checked_out_dir()
            self._make_out_dir(out)

                comparison = compare_backups(out / 'backup_a.bin',
                                             out / 'backup_b.bin',
                                             evidence['parsed']['capacity'])
                result['comparison'] = comparison
                result['passed'] = True
        except BaseException as error:
            result['error'] = repr(error)
            result['passed'] = False
        finally:
            result['finished_unix'] = time.time()
            self._write_result(result)
        return result

    def _one_dump(self, name, evidence, out, result):
        """Run one dump pass; its log and its partial file are always kept."""
        capacity = evidence['parsed']['capacity']
        target_file = out / ('backup_%s.bin' % name)
        log_file = out / ('backup_%s.log' % name)
        if target_file.exists() or target_file.is_symlink():
            raise FlashError('refusing to overwrite the existing dump %s' % target_file)
        argv = build_command('dump', self.tool, output=target_file, size=capacity)
        info = {'command': [str(item) for item in argv], 'log': str(log_file),
                'file': str(target_file), 'returncode': None, 'timeout': False,
                'error': None}
        result['dumps'][name] = info
        self._run_logged(argv, log_file, self._timeout_for('dump'), info)
        if info['error']:
            raise FlashError('dump %s: %s' % (name, info['error']))
        if info['returncode'] != 0:
            raise FlashError('dump %s exited with %s' % (name, info['returncode']))
        parsed = parse_dump_log(log_file.read_bytes(),
                                 jedec=evidence['parsed']['jedec'],
                                 sectors=evidence['parsed']['sectors'])

    """Normalize the reviewed guard identity into the recorded target."""
    identity = dict(identity or {})
    target = dict(identity.get('target') or {})
    return {'serial': target.get('serial') or identity.get('target_serial'),
            'idVendor': target.get('idVendor'), 'idProduct': target.get('idProduct'),
            'busnum': target.get('busnum'), 'devnum': target.get('devnum'),
            'path': target.get('path'),
            'board': identity.get('board') or target.get('board')}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _install_signal_handlers():
    """Cooperative handlers: the finally block still writes the JSON."""
    previous = {}

    def handler(signum, _frame):
        raise _Abort('signal %d' % signum)

    for number in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGHUP):
        try:
            previous[number] = signal.signal(number, handler)
        except (ValueError, OSError):
            pass
    return previous


def _restore_signal_handlers(previous):
    for number, old in previous.items():
        try:
            signal.signal(number, old)
        except (ValueError, OSError):
            pass


def build_parser():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog='flash_readonly.py',
        description='Root-only flash detect and double read-only backup coordinator.')
    parser.add_argument('--phase', choices=('detect', 'dump'), default='detect')
    parser.add_argument('--out', type=Path, required=True,
                        help='exclusive output directory, ROOT/TESTS/NEW')
    parser.add_argument('--run', action='store_true',
                        help='execute the reviewed steps (default: prepare only)')
    parser.add_argument('--timeout', type=int, default=None,
                        help='seconds per command, %d..%d' % (MIN_TIMEOUT, MAX_TIMEOUT))
    parser.add_argument('--detection', type=Path, default=None,
                        help='detection JSON of the detect phase')
    parser.add_argument('--detection-sha', default=None,
                        help='exact SHA-256 of the detection JSON')
    parser.add_argument('--jedec', default=None, help='JEDEC ID observed by root')
    parser.add_argument('--capacity', type=int, default=None,
                        help='capacity in bytes observed by root')
    # No --root and no PRODOCK_ROOT: the production root is the pinned one.
    # An internal constructor argument may inject a root for the fakes.
    return parser


def main(argv=None, runner=None, guard_factory=None):
    """Entry point. Returns 0 on success, 1 on a failed phase, 2 on a refusal."""
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.timeout is not None and not (MIN_TIMEOUT <= args.timeout <= MAX_TIMEOUT):
        print(json.dumps({'error': 'timeout must be between %d and %d seconds'
                                  % (MIN_TIMEOUT, MAX_TIMEOUT)}, indent=2))
        return 2
    try:
        coordinator = Coordinator(
            phase=args.phase, out_dir=args.out, root=ROOT, timeout=args.timeout,
            runner=runner, guard_factory=guard_factory, detection=args.detection,
            detection_sha=args.detection_sha, jedec=args.jedec, capacity=args.capacity)
    except FlashError as error:
        print(json.dumps({'error': repr(error)}, indent=2))
        return 2

    if not args.run:
        try:
            plan = coordinator.prepare()
        except FlashError as error:
            print(json.dumps({'phase': args.phase, 'mode': 'prepare',
                              'error': repr(error)}, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
            return 2
        print(json.dumps(plan, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
        return 0

    previous = _install_signal_handlers()
    try:
        result = coordinator.execute()
    except _Abort as error:
        print(json.dumps({'error': repr(error)}, indent=2))
        return 130
    finally:
        _restore_signal_handlers(previous)
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    return 0 if result.get('passed') else 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

class FakeGuard:
    """Stand-in for the reviewed guarded_target() context manager."""

    def __init__(self, state, on_enter=None):
        self.state = state
        self.on_enter = on_enter

    def __enter__(self):
        self.state['entries'] += 1
        self.state['held'] += 1
        if self.on_enter is not None:
            self.on_enter()
        return {'target_serial': fr.SERIAL,
                'target': {'serial': fr.SERIAL, 'idVendor': fr.VENDOR,
                           'idProduct': fr.PRODUCT, 'busnum': 1, 'devnum': 4,
                           'path': '1-1.4'},
                'board': fr.BOARD}

    def __exit__(self, *exc_info):
        self.state['held'] -= 1
        self.state['exits'] += 1
        return False


class FakeRunner:
    """Stand-in for the real subprocess runner.

    A step is a dict with the optional keys 'log' (bytes written into the
    tool log), 'file' (bytes written into the dump file, exactly like the
    tool does), 'rc' (return code) and 'raise' (an exception to raise).
    """

    def __init__(self, state, steps):
        self.state = state
        self.steps = list(steps)

    def __call__(self, argv, stdout, timeout):
        self.state['argv'].append(list(argv))
        self.state['timeouts'].append(timeout)
        self.state['held_when_called'].append(self.state['held'])
        step = self.steps.pop(0) if self.steps else {}
        payload = step.get('log')
        if payload:
            stdout.write(payload)
        if step.get('file') is not None:
            Path(argv[-1]).write_bytes(step['file'])
        if 'raise' in step:
            raise step['raise']
        return step.get('rc', 0)

    def setUp(self):

                      'timeouts': [], 'held_when_called': []}

    # -- fakes ------------------------------------------------------------
    def guard(self, on_enter=None):
        return lambda: FakeGuard(self.state, on_enter)

    def runner(self, steps):
        return FakeRunner(self.state, steps)

    # -- helpers ----------------------------------------------------------
    def coordinator(self, phase, out_dir, runner, **kwargs):

                              runner=runner, guard_factory=self.guard(),

            Path(fr.__file__).resolve().parent / fr.GUARD_RELATIVE))

    def test_no_command_outside_the_allowlist(self):
        _detect_out, detection, _result = self.run_detect()
        out = self.root / 'TESTS' / 'dump-allowlist'
        runner = self.runner([{'log': DUMP_LOG, 'rc': 0, 'file': PAYLOAD},
                              {'log': DUMP_LOG, 'rc': 0, 'file': PAYLOAD}])
        self.coordinator('dump', out, runner, detection=detection,
                         detection_sha=fr.sha256_file(detection), jedec=JEDEC,
                         capacity=CAPACITY).execute()

        forbidden = ('--bulk-erase', '--unprotect-flash', '--erase',
                     '--verify', '--program')
        for argv in self.state['argv']:
            self.assertEqual(argv[0], str(self.root / 'bin' / 'openFPGALoader'))
            self.assertEqual(argv[argv.index('--usb-serial-num') + 1], fr.SERIAL)
            self.assertEqual(argv[argv.index('-b') + 1], fr.BOARD)
            self.assertIn('--verbose', argv)
            for flag in forbidden:
                self.assertNotIn(flag, argv)
            if '--write-flash' in argv:
                # The only allowed write flag is the non writing detect mode.
                self.assertIn('--detect', argv)
                self.assertEqual(argv[-1], '--detect')
            if '--dump-flash' in argv:
                self.assertEqual(argv[argv.index('--file-size') + 1],
                                 str(CAPACITY))
                self.assertNotIn('--write-flash', argv)

    def test_prepare_of_the_dump_phase_after_a_fake_detect(self):
        _detect_out, detection, _result = self.run_detect()
        out = self.root / 'TESTS' / 'dump-plan'
        coordinator = self.coordinator(
            'dump', out, self.runner([]), detection=detection,
            detection_sha=fr.sha256_file(detection), jedec=JEDEC,
            capacity=CAPACITY)
        before = len(self.state['argv'])
        plan = coordinator.prepare()
        self.assertEqual(len(plan['commands']), 2)
        self.assertEqual(plan['commands'][0][plan['commands'][0].index('--file-size') + 1],
                         str(CAPACITY))
        self.assertEqual(plan['detection']['capacity'], CAPACITY)
        self.assertTrue(plan['sram_interrupt_expected'])
        # Prepare opens no resource and creates no file.
        self.assertFalse(out.exists())
        self.assertEqual(len(self.state['argv']), before)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
"}

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline flash preparation and exact readback checks; no device access.

Only ordinary flash bytes are backed up, not OTP/security/status registers.
A 64 KiB-aligned image preserves the remainder of the last erased sector.
Full-capacity readback also checks all bytes beyond the programmed region.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import stat
from pathlib import Path


def digest(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def read_regular(path, expected_size=None):
    path = Path(path)
    mode = path.lstat().st_mode
    if not stat.S_ISREG(mode):
        raise ValueError(f"Not a regular non-symlink file: {path}")
    data = path.read_bytes()
    if expected_size is not None and len(data) != expected_size:
        raise ValueError(f"Wrong length for {path}: {len(data)} != {expected_size}")
    return data


def prepare(payload_path, backup_a, backup_b, capacity, output):
    """Require two exact, independent full dumps before generating an image.

    Caller must retain each dump's separate hardware log. Equality alone does
    not attest that a file was read from the intended chip; this is offline.
    """
    if not 65536 <= capacity <= 64 * 1024 * 1024 or capacity % 65536:
        raise ValueError("Capacity must come from identified flash geometry")
    if Path(backup_a).resolve() == Path(backup_b).resolve():
        raise ValueError("Two distinct backup files are required")
    if Path(backup_a).samefile(backup_b):
        raise ValueError("Backups cannot be hard links to one file")
    a = read_regular(backup_a, capacity)
    b = read_regular(backup_b, capacity)
    if a != b:
        raise ValueError("Independent backups disagree")
    payload = read_regular(payload_path)
    if not 0 < len(payload) <= capacity:
        raise ValueError("Payload does not fit")
    end = (len(payload) + 65535) & ~65535
    image = payload + a[len(payload):end]
    expected = payload + a[len(payload):]
    output = Path(output)
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    (output / 'program.bin').write_bytes(image)
    # Only a hash is needed for the full expected image: no duplicate backup.
    report = dict(schema=1, hardware_access=False, capacity=capacity,
                  backup_sha256=digest(a), payload_sha256=digest(payload),
                  payload_bytes=len(payload), program_bytes=len(image),
                  program_sha256=digest(image), expected_full_sha256=digest(expected),
                  preserved_last_sector_bytes=end-len(payload),
                  preserved_tail_bytes=capacity-len(payload))
    (output / 'plan.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + '\n')
    return report


def verify(plan_path, dump_path):
    plan = json.loads(read_regular(plan_path))
    dump = read_regular(dump_path, plan['capacity'])
    actual = digest(dump)
    if actual != plan['expected_full_sha256']:
        raise ValueError("Full flash readback differs from intended bytes")
    return dict(full_readback_matches=True, bytes=len(dump), sha256=actual,
                hardware_boot_tested=False, powercycle_tested=False)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    subs = parser.add_subparsers(dest='action', required=True)
    prep = subs.add_parser('prepare')
    for name in ('payload', 'backup-a', 'backup-b', 'out'):
        prep.add_argument('--' + name, type=Path, required=True)
    prep.add_argument('--capacity', type=int, required=True)
    check = subs.add_parser('verify')
    check.add_argument('--plan', type=Path, required=True)
    check.add_argument('--dump', type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.action == 'prepare':
        result = prepare(args.payload, args.backup_a, args.backup_b, args.capacity, args.out)
    else:
        result = verify(args.plan, args.dump)
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
"}

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Strict grammar of the Gowin external flash program log.

Scope
-----
``parse_program`` decides whether the log of one ``--write-flash --verify``
pass really shows a completed write *and* a completed internal verification.
It never judges the exit code of the tool: a zero exit status is a separate
fact that the caller checks on its own.

Grammar
-------
The real ``Gowin::programExtFlash`` initialises the SPI flash (one
``read_id``) and then reads the identification again explicitly, so the log
may carry **one or two** JEDEC / geometry records.  Two records are accepted
only when they are identical; disagreeing records are a refusal.  The
physical chain stays unique: one ``found 1 devices``, one ``index 0:`` and
the idcode 0x1081b of the tangmega138k.

The accepted order is exactly:

    Writing ... 100.00%
    Done
    Verifying write (May take time)
    Reading ... 100.00%
    Done

A completion line that is followed by a device or flash record is refused,
and so is any error word (except the narrowly documented historical
``auto_boot_1st_fail`` flag of the read-only coordinator).

The text ``after program flash`` is printed *before* the operation starts;
it is therefore never accepted as evidence of anything.  This module only
reports whether it was present.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# The sibling module is loaded from this very directory, whatever the cwd is.
_HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
if str(_HERE) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(_HERE))

import proofs  # noqa: E402  (local module, loaded from this directory only)

ANSI_RE = re.compile(r'\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[ -/]*[@-~]'
                      r'|\x1b\][^\x07\x1b]*(?:\x07|\x1b\\)'
                      r'|\x1b[@-Z\\-_]')

WRITING_RE = re.compile(r'^\s*writing\b[^\n]*?(?<![\d.])100\.00\s*%[^\n]*$', re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE)
READING_RE = re.compile(r'^\s*reading\b[^\n]*?(?<![\d.])100\.00\s*%[^\n]*$', re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE)
VERIFY_RE = re.compile(r'verifying\s+write(?:\s*\(\s*may\s+take\s+time\s*\))?',
                       re.IGNORECASE)
AFTER_PROGRAM_RE = re.compile(r'after\s+program\s+flash', re.IGNORECASE)



def _as_text(raw):
    """Decode a log to text without ever raising on odd bytes."""
    if isinstance(raw, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
        return bytes(raw).decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    return str(raw)


def _normalise(raw):
    """Drop ANSI colour sequences and turn progress carriage returns into lines."""
    text = _as_text(raw).replace('\r\n', '\n').replace('\r', '\n')
    return ANSI_RE.sub('', text)


def _done_lines(lines):
    """Indices of the bare "Done" completion lines."""
    return [index for index, line in enumerate(lines) if line.strip() == 'Done']


def _records(text, pattern, what):
    """Return every match of `pattern` in the text."""
    return list(pattern.finditer(text))


def _line_index(text, position):
    """Line index of a character position."""
    return text.count('\n', 0, position)


def _check_identification(readonly, text, jedec, sectors):
    """Validate the unique physical chain and the JEDEC / geometry records.

    One or two identical JEDEC and geometry records are accepted, because the
    reviewed program path reads the flash identification twice.
    """
    what = 'program log'
    readonly._check_physical_header(text, what)

    jedec_any = readonly.JEDEC_ANY_RE.findall(text)
    if len(jedec_any) not in (1, 2):
        raise proofs.ProofError('%s: expected one or two JEDEC ID records, got %d'
                                % (what, len(jedec_any)))
    jedec_matches = readonly.JEDEC_RE.findall(text)
    if len(jedec_matches) != len(jedec_any):
        raise proofs.ProofError('%s: unsupported flash identification %r'
                                % (what, jedec_any))
    observed = {value.lower() for value in jedec_matches}
    if len(observed) != 1:
        raise proofs.ProofError('%s: the two JEDEC records disagree: %r'
                                % (what, sorted(observed)))
    jedec_value = observed.pop()
    expected_jedec = str(jedec).strip().lower()
    if jedec_value != expected_jedec:
        raise proofs.ProofError('%s: JEDEC %s differs from the expected %s'
                                % (what, jedec_value, expected_jedec))

    detected = readonly.DETECTED_LINE_RE.findall(text)
    if len(detected) != len(jedec_matches):
        raise proofs.ProofError('%s: expected one or two "Detected:" flash records,'
                                ' got %d' % (what, len(detected)))
    models = []
    sector_counts = []
    for line in detected:
        model, count, _size = readonly._parse_detected(line, what)
        models.append(model)
        sector_counts.append(count)
    if len(set(models)) != 1:
        raise proofs.ProofError('%s: the two flash records disagree on the model: %r'
                                % (what, models))
    if len(set(sector_counts)) != 1:
        raise proofs.ProofError('%s: the two flash records disagree on the geometry'
                                % (what, sector_counts))
    if sector_counts[0] != int(sectors):
        raise proofs.ProofError('%s: %d sectors differ from the expected %s'
                                % (what, sector_counts[0], sectors))
    return {'jedec': jedec_value, 'model': models[0], 'sectors': sector_counts[0],
            'capacity': sector_counts[0] * proofs.SECTOR_BYTES,
            'jedec_records': len(jedec_matches), 'detected_records': len(detected)}


def _check_phases(readonly, text, lines):
    """Require the write phase, then the internal verification, in order."""
    what = 'program log'
    writing = _records(text, WRITING_RE, what)
    reading = _records(text, READING_RE, what)
    verify = _records(text, VERIFY_RE, what)
    if not writing or not reading or len(verify) != 1:
        raise proofs.ProofError('Expected write progress and one verification phase')
    write_lines = [_line_index(text, m.start()) for m in writing]
    read_lines = [_line_index(text, m.start()) for m in reading]
    write_at, read_at = write_lines[0], read_lines[0]
    verify_at = _line_index(text, verify[0].start())
    if not write_at < verify_at < read_at:
        raise proofs.ProofError('Write and verification are not in order')
    # The last non-forced sample may round to 100.00%, before done() prints
    # exactly 100.00% again. Accept repeated progress, never a second Done.
    dones = _done_lines(lines)
    write_done = [i for i in dones if write_at < i < verify_at]
    final_done = [i for i in dones if i > read_at]
    if len(write_done) != 1 or len(final_done) != 1:
        raise proofs.ProofError('Each write/verify phase requires exactly one Done')
    write_done, final_done = write_done[0], final_done[0]
    if any(i >= write_done for i in write_lines) or any(i <= verify_at or i >= final_done for i in read_lines):
        raise proofs.ProofError('Progress crosses a completed phase')
    for pattern in (readonly.JEDEC_ANY_RE, readonly.DETECTED_LINE_RE,
                    readonly.FOUND_RE, readonly.INDEX_RE, readonly.IDCODE_RE):
        if any(_line_index(text, m.start()) >= write_at for m in pattern.finditer(text)):
            raise proofs.ProofError('Identification appears after writing began')
    for line in lines[final_done + 1:]:
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if readonly._is_significant(line):
            raise proofs.ProofError('%s: a device or flash record follows the final '
                                    '"Done" line' % what)
    return {'write_done_line': write_done, 'final_done_line': final_done,
            'write_progress_line': write_at, 'verify_line': verify_at,
            'read_progress_line': read_at}


def parse_program(raw, *, jedec, sectors):
    """Parse a program log into a strict summary.

    Raises ``ProofError`` (a ValueError, RuntimeError and OSError) for an
    unknown or inconsistent identification, a missing write or verification
    phase, an out of order sequence, an error word or a record that follows
    the completion line.
    """
    readonly = proofs.flash_readonly()
    text = _normalise(raw)
    lines = text.splitlines()
    what = 'program log'

    context = readonly._error_context(text)
    if context:
        raise proofs.ProofError('%s reports an error status: %r' % (what, context))

    summary = _check_identification(readonly, text, jedec, sectors)
    summary.update(_check_phases(readonly, text, lines))
    summary['write_verified'] = True
    summary['verify_observed'] = True
    summary['after_program_flash_text'] = bool(AFTER_PROGRAM_RE.search(text))
    summary['bytes'] = len(_as_text(raw))
    return summary
"}

{"content": """"Independent fake evidence generated by the frozen readonly coordinator.

No device access. The small geometry is a synthetic log fixture, not a claim
about a physical W25Q128 capacity. Tests use injected target/runner boundaries.
"""
import contextlib
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path

CAPACITY = 4 * 65536
SECTORS = 4
JEDEC = 'ef4018'
IDENT = b'found 1 devices\nindex 0:\n idcode 0x1081b\n'
FLASH = b'JEDEC ID: 0xef4018\nDetected: winbond W25Q128 4 sectors size: 2Mb\n'
DETECT = IDENT + b'Detect flash:\n' + FLASH + b'Done\n'
DUMP = IDENT + FLASH + (b'dump flash (May take time)\nOpen dump file DONE\n'
                        b'Read flash 100.00%\nDone\n')
PROGRAM = IDENT + FLASH + FLASH + (b'Writing: [========] 100.00%\nDone\n'
                                   b'Verifying write (May take time)\n'
                                   b'Reading: [========] 100.00%\nDone\n')
BACKUP = bytes(range(256)) * (CAPACITY // 256)


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def store(path, value):
    Path(path).write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2) + '\n')
    return {'path': str(path), 'sha256': sha(path)}


class Fixture:
    def __init__(self, root, source):
        self.root = Path(root)
        self.tests = self.root / 'TESTS'
        self.tests.mkdir()
        self.source = Path(source)
        self.calls = []
        self.held = False
        path = self.source / 'refs/readonly/flash_readonly.py'
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('review_readonly', path)
        self.ro = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(self.ro)
        # Real readonly orchestration and validation; only I/O boundaries fake.
        detect = self.tests / 'detect'
        result = self.ro.Coordinator(phase='detect', root=self.root, out_dir=detect,
            runner=self.runner, guard_factory=self.guard).execute()
        assert result['passed'], result
        self.detection = detect / 'detect.json'
        dump = self.tests / 'backup'
        result = self.ro.Coordinator(phase='dump', root=self.root, out_dir=dump,
            runner=self.runner, guard_factory=self.guard, detection=self.detection,
            detection_sha=sha(self.detection), jedec=JEDEC, capacity=CAPACITY).execute()
        assert result['passed'], result
        self.backup_result = dump / 'dump.json'
        self.fs = self.tests / 'candidate.fs'
        self.fs.write_bytes((self.source / 'fixture.fs').read_bytes())
        self.sram = self.tests / 'sram.json'
        sram_ref = store(self.sram, {
            'target_serial': '2025071717', 'bitstream_sha256': sha(self.fs),
            'configuration_completed': True, 'flash_writes': 0,
            'physical_idcodes': ['1081b'], 'programmer_reaped': True,
            'passed': True, 'log_checks_passed': True, 'game_launch_observed': True,
            'fresh_console_observed': True})
        self.acceptance = self.tests / 'root_acceptance.json'
        acc_ref = store(self.acceptance, {
            'target_serial': '2025071717', 'physical_idcode': '0001081b',
            'bitstream_sha256': sha(self.fs), 'sram_result_sha256': sha(self.sram),
            'dump_result_sha256': sha(self.backup_result), 'sram_boot_accepted': True,
            'permission_to_program': True, 'flash_unchanged_since_backup': True})
        self.request = self.tests / 'request.json'
        self.req = {
            'version': 1, 'target_serial': '2025071717', 'physical_idcode': '0001081b',
            'bitstream': {'path': str(self.fs), 'sha256': sha(self.fs)},
            'sram_result': sram_ref,
            'detection': {'path': str(self.detection), 'sha256': sha(self.detection)},
            'backups': {'path': str(self.backup_result), 'sha256': sha(self.backup_result)},
            'acceptance': acc_ref, 'jedec': JEDEC, 'capacity': CAPACITY}
        self.sync()
        self.calls.clear()
        self.after = None
        self.program_fault = None
        self.dump_fault = None

    def sync(self):
        store(self.request, self.req)

    @contextlib.contextmanager
    def guard(self):
        assert not self.held
        self.held = True
        try:
            yield {'target_serial': '2025071717', 'board': 'tangmega138k',
                   'target': {'serial': '2025071717', 'idVendor': '0403',
                              'idProduct': '6010', 'busnum': 3, 'devnum': 12}}
        finally:
            self.held = False

    def runner(self, argv, stdout, timeout):
        assert self.held, 'runner invoked without the shared lock'
        self.calls.append(list(argv))
        assert argv[argv.index('--usb-serial-num') + 1] == '2025071717'
        if '--detect' in argv:
            stdout.write(DETECT)
        elif '--dump-flash' in argv:
            fault = getattr(self, 'dump_fault', None)
            if fault:
                raise fault
            stdout.write(DUMP)
            Path(argv[-1]).write_bytes(getattr(self, 'after', None) or BACKUP)
        elif '--write-flash' in argv:
            assert '--verify' in argv
            fault = getattr(self, 'program_fault', None)
            if fault:
                raise fault
            stdout.write(PROGRAM)
        else:
            raise AssertionError(argv)
        return 0
"}

{"content": "# Préparation flash de la nouvelle Pro Dock — aucune opération carte exécutée

Cible unique : **FT2232 `2025071717`, GW5AST-138B / PG676**, sur ax15.
La Pro Dock `2023112818` et le J-Link `506005083` sont exclus de cette procédure.
Le candidat doit d'abord être essayé en SRAM par root. Le présent dossier ne
qualifie aucun bitstream, aucune flash, ni un démarrage après coupure secteur.

## Ce que les sources établissent

Source locale propre : `/home/michael/openFPGALoader-src`, commit
`24e46d13bb8f2bc9371e9ca8443ece2fafc4b20d`, binaire annoncé `v1.1.1`, SHA-256
`101c3c17456644f08217c3b11103aa78f8ab4debf4d2d133831c9c91c6d6d873`.
Les empreintes des fichiers effectivement lus figurent dans `provenance.json`.
Root a depuis relevé sur ax15 le **même SHA du binaire runtime** et la même
version. Le lanceur `bin/openFPGALoader` a pour SHA
`1c0c245f4bcad2c537b5fbaf77d055c5eccf6b3b17835a24c79be631cd218066` ; il
fixe `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` sur `runtime/lib`, puis exécute `runtime/openFPGALoader`.
Cette association est une mesure communiquée par root, pas une interrogation
effectuée par cet agent. Vérifier les deux SHA avant les opérations.

La documentation officielle annonce la flash externe pour GW5AST-138. La
ligne carte `tangmega138k`, elle, affiche encore Flash « TBD » : le support
logiciel de la famille ne vaut donc pas qualification de notre carte.
[Table FPGA](https://trabucayre.github.io/openFPGALoader/compatibility/fpga.html),
[table cartes](https://trabucayre.github.io/openFPGALoader/compatibility/board.html).

| Source du commit examiné | Constat précis |
|---|---|
| `src/part.hpp`, `src/board.hpp` | ID `0001081b` = GW5AST-138 ; `tangmega138k` utilise FT2232/SPI_FLASH. |
| `src/gowin.cpp:218` | GW5AST sélectionne automatiquement la flash externe. `skip_checksum` vise le checksum USER du FPGA, pas la comparaison SPI. |
| `src/gowin.cpp:342` | `programExtFlash()` efface/programme, puis `SPIFlash::verify(...,256)` si demandé ; une erreur propagée lève une exception. |
| `src/gowin.cpp:100`, `src/rawParser.cpp:19` | `.fs` → `FsParser(false)` ; `.bin` → `RawParser(false)`. Ce dernier copie les octets sans inversion ni en-tête ajouté. Les deux passent le même `getData(),getLength()/8` à la routine SPI. |
| `src/spiFlash.cpp:559` | La vérification SPI relit et compare chaque octet de la plage programmée. Elle ne prouve ni boot, ni fonctionnement Linux/GPU. |
| `src/gowin.cpp:1220` | **Préparer un accès flash efface la SRAM FPGA** sur GW5A. Le retour désactive SPI et réinitialise le FPGA. Détection et dump ont aussi cet effet. |
| `src/main.cpp:678` | Le booléen rendu par `dumpFlash()`/`detect_flash()` n'est pas exploité. Un exit 0 ne suffit pas. |
| `src/spiFlash.cpp:325` | Le dump vérifie les lectures SPI, mais pas les retours `fwrite()` et `fclose()`. D'où taille + SHA + deuxième lecture indépendante. |
| `src/spiFlash.cpp:207` | Effacement arrondi à 4 KiB ou 64 KiB selon le composant. La fin du secteur peut être effacée hors de la longueur du `.fs`. |

Références de code stables :
[Gowin](https://github.com/trabucayre/openFPGALoader/blob/24e46d13bb8f2bc9371e9ca8443ece2fafc4b20d/src/gowin.cpp),
[SPIFlash](https://github.com/trabucayre/openFPGALoader/blob/24e46d13bb8f2bc9371e9ca8443ece2fafc4b20d/src/spiFlash.cpp),
[main](https://github.com/trabucayre/openFPGALoader/blob/24e46d13bb8f2bc9371e9ca8443ece2fafc4b20d/src/main.cpp).

`--skip-reset` ne préserve pas la configuration dans cette implémentation
Gowin. Aucun `--bulk-erase`, `--unprotect-flash` ou accès OTP/security n'est
prévu. Un blocage de protection doit être examiné, pas contourné automatiquement.
La sauvegarde concerne l'espace mémoire SPI ordinaire ; elle ne capture pas
les fusibles, OTP, registres de protection ou registres d'état du composant.

## Séquence proposée à root

1. Finir l'essai SRAM du candidat exact et conserver son SHA et le résultat
   `target_serial=2025071717`, `configuration_completed=true`, `flash_writes=0`.
   Préparer ensuite l'arrêt contrôlé de ce Linux, s'il fonctionne. Tout accès
   flash ci-dessous interrompra cette configuration et pourra recharger le
   programme actuellement en flash. Il ne faut pas lancer le dump pendant une
   mesure ou une écriture SD du candidat.
2. Identifier le binaire ax15 par `sha256sum` et `--version` (pas de JTAG).
